name: EXP-LIFE-002 One commit verb, driven by the git adapter, so delivery and seal stop needing parameters
goal:
EXP-LIFE-002 — One commit verb, driven by the git adapter, so delivery and seal stop needing parameters

OPERATOR REQUEST (2026-10-14, in substance): "I don't want to add a million new verbs all the time...
since we will do an actual integration of the git adapter I think we could drive all that preparation
when committing, so maybe something like `synth expedition consolidate` or `synth expedition commit`
which will do whatever we need to do before any commit, the actual commit, and any post commit stuff
we may like."

PREMISE AND HARD DEPENDENCY: the CLI verbs get fixed FIRST. This expedition depends on EXP-CLI-003
(e47a186cb472a20a), which replaces the 9121-line switch in src/cli/synth.ts with a verb -> loader
registry and enforces a load budget. Adding a verb to the monolith now would mean adding it twice,
and would grow the graph that EXP-CLI-003 exists to shrink. `consolidate` is therefore registered in
the registry, never in the switch. EXP-LIFE-001 (73c5c033360fecf3) is the SOURCE of the findings
below but deliberately not a dependency: it is an audit expedition that may never execute, and
blocking this work on it would block it forever.

THE NAMING CONSTRAINT IS ALREADY BINDING. `synth expedition commit` EXISTS and means something else:
the approved -> committed lifecycle transition (`--proposal-id`, `--all-approved --mission`,
`--branch`, `--no-create`, `--dry-run`; ADR-056 §2.3 forbids two expeditions sharing one branch). It
is not a git commit. So the operator's first-choice name is taken, and taking it anyway would put two
meanings of "commit" one subcommand apart. The verb is `consolidate`. The expedition verb count today
is already 17+ (create, new, approve, commit, start, complete, finish, cancel, archive, delete, move,
evidence, refine, certify, deliver, seal, abandon) — this expedition adds exactly ONE and removes
duplicated commit logic from the others.

WHY: THE DEFECT, MEASURED THIS SESSION
Closing out EXP-CLI-001 (2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) after PR #345 merged required an operator to supply two
parameters the ledger could have derived, and one of them failed:

  * `deliver --branch origin/arena/15e0fc51-synth` returned DELIVERY_PUSH_FAILED: "Could not push
    origin/arena/15e0fc51-synth to origin: Branch origin/arena/15e0fc51-synth does not exist locally
    or on origin" — for a branch `git ls-remote` confirms IS on origin. The verb's default action is
    to PUSH, and `pushBranch` rejects the very `origin/<name>` form that `resolveDeliveryBranch`
    (src/ledger/delivery.ts:254) itself produces while separately computing `canonicalBranch` with the
    prefix stripped. Resolution and pushing disagree about what a branch name is. `--no-push` is the
    documented escape hatch and is what worked.
  * `seal` demanded `--merge-commit <sha>` — a value the operator has to leave the ledger and read off
    GitHub. It is derivable from data the ledger already holds.
  * Neither verb commits. Both wrote canonical-state.json, two event-stream partitions and the
    expedition record, then left the tree dirty for `synth doctor` to report as `ledgerCeremony`.
    Meanwhile `refine`, `start` and `complete` DO auto-commit, each building its own pathspec list —
    which is how commit 5907889 swept 1578 lines of proof/certifications byproduct into history even
    though AUTO_COMMIT_INCLUDE_ROOTS (src/state/artifact-policy.ts:105) says
    [".synth/data", "proof/expeditions", "AGENTS.md"]. Two competing definitions of commit scope, and
    the broader one won. EXP-CLEAN-001 D6(b) records the same leak from the other side; this
    expedition is where it gets fixed, and CLEAN-001's D6 deliverable should be reduced accordingly.

THE INSIGHT THAT MAKES THIS SMALL: seal's only real assertion is CONTAINMENT — "is the work I said I
did actually on main?" — and the ledger already stores the work as a hash
(`metadata.delivery.tipCommit`). Verified against every expedition that has one (4 of 4):

    git merge-base --is-ancestor <tipCommit> main                                  -> containment
    git rev-list --ancestry-path --merges --reverse <tipCommit>..main | head -1    -> the merge commit

  That derivation reproduced, exactly and with no human input, the sha I had looked up on GitHub and
  typed by hand: 2c13ca22 -> 12884da29307 (== the `--merge-commit` supplied manually), 2c9c6c62 ->
  8b8dce269258 (== PR #344's merge), 87e6515d -> 12f1bce56b73, f0f81e35 -> 21ffc64986e6.
  Caveat, stated because it will bite: with stacked merges the derivation returns the FIRST merge
  containing the tip, which can be an intermediate merge rather than the PR merge — f0f81e35 derives
  21ffc64, itself a parent of #343's bb8809ae. Containment is unaffected; only the decorative sha
  differs. `--merge-commit` therefore survives as an optional OVERRIDE, never as a requirement.

THE BACKLOG THIS UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: 34 expeditions are `completed` and only 4 are sealed, so 30 are
completed-but-unsealed. Of those 30, none has a recorded tipCommit (they predate the discipline), so
each needs derivation: 18 can be tied to a merge commit using nothing but main's observable contents
(the PR merge message names the branch, and the branch name carries the expedition id), and 12 cannot
be tied to anything on main at all (e.g. d0a701df55ef36d7, branch
expedition/9861cf62476c90ae/d0a701df55ef36d7) — those are ARCHIVE candidates, not seal candidates,
because there is no evidence their work landed. This supersedes the earlier 24/6 estimate in
EXP-LIFE-001 finding H, which used a looser derivation; under a "justified from main's observable
contents only" rule the honest split is 18/12.

THE SPEC (operator, standing): the no-VCS thought experiment. Any parameter the no-VCS world doesn't
need is a parameter the ledger must not require. In a world without git there is no branch name and no
merge commit — there is only "here is all my work" and "someone with authority accepted it". Measured
against that spec, `deliver --branch` and `seal --merge-commit` both fail today, and `deliver`'s push
fails worst of all: pushing is an ACTION, not an assertion, and it is the one part that broke.

DELIVERABLES
  D1. `synth expedition consolidate` — ONE new verb, three phases, driven through the git adapter:
        PRE     decide what belongs in the commit from ONE authority (the artifact classification in
                src/state/artifact-policy.ts), validate the tree, refuse to sweep byproducts;
        COMMIT  create the commit through `GitRepositoryAdapter` (src/adapters/repository/git.ts:64,
                factory at :747) rather than a fresh child_process git call — this is the "actual
                integration of the git adapter" the operator asked for;
        POST    record the resulting work hash on the expedition, append the ceremony event, and
                report what it compared.
      Support `--dry-run` that is genuinely read-only (unlike `seal --dry-run`, which WRITES —
      EXP-LIFE-001 finding A) and `--message`/`--paths` overrides.
  D2. `consolidate` becomes the SINGLE commit authority. The per-verb auto-commit paths
      (src/ledger/ceremony.ts:339-366 builds its `existing` pathspec list from whatever its caller
      passes; src/ledger/writer.ts:523 likewise) collapse into it. `refine`, `start`, `complete`,
      `finish`, `certify` keep their `--no-auto-commit` opt-out but call the same code. No verb keeps
      a private notion of what a ceremony commit may contain.
  D3. "Here is all my work" is recorded as a hash at commit time, so containment is a comparison
      instead of an archaeology. Every expedition that reaches `completed` carries the tip it was
      completed at.
  D4. `deliver` becomes a pure assertion: no push by default (push becomes opt-in `--push`),
      `--branch` optional (fall back to the recorded execution branch, then the EXPEDITION_BRANCH_CREATED
      event, then a remote ref naming the id — the candidate order `resolveDeliveryBranch` already
      implements), and the record stores the CANONICAL branch name, not a ref path. That fixes
      EXP-LIFE-001 finding G at the source; both existing records (2c13ca22, 2c9c6c62) show the
      `origin/`-prefixed form.
  D5. `seal` requires nothing but `--id`: fetch main (a READ — the only irreducible VCS contact),
      assert containment of the recorded tip, derive and store the integrating merge, and print what
      it compared. If it cannot fetch, it must REFUSE rather than assert — the behaviour I had to
      apply by hand when GitHub was unreachable mid-session. `--merge-commit` stays as an override for
      stacked merges.
  D6. Close the backlog with the derived, guarded procedure: seal the 18 whose integration is
      justified from main's observable contents, archive the 12 that cannot be tied to main, and
      publish both lists with the evidence line for each. No expedition is sealed on a guess.

ACCEPTANCE
  * Exactly one verb is added. `synth expedition --help` lists `consolidate` and still lists
    `commit` with its unchanged lifecycle meaning; the two are documented as different things in the
    help text so the collision cannot confuse the next agent.
  * `synth expedition seal --id <id>` with NO other parameters seals an expedition whose tip is on
    main, and stores a derived merge commit equal to the one an operator would have supplied. Proved
    on a real expedition, not a fixture.
  * `synth expedition deliver --id <id>` with NO other parameters records a delivery, does not push,
    and stores a canonical branch name with no `origin/` prefix.
  * `seal` refuses (non-zero, no write) when main cannot be fetched; proved by breaking connectivity
    or pointing at an unreachable remote.
  * `consolidate --dry-run` writes nothing: tree and event count identical before and after.
  * Commit scope has ONE authority: re-running the 5907889 scenario (a full chain run leaving
    proof/certifications byproducts, then a ceremony commit) stages ledger paths only. A test asserts
    it, chained.
  * All 30 completed-but-unsealed expeditions are resolved: 18 sealed, 12 archived, each with its
    evidence line, and the counts reconciled against the measurement above.
  * `npm run test:all` green with the new tests chained; `synth verify` ok; `synth doctor` 12/12;
    `npm run audit:module-graph` shows the dispatcher graph did NOT grow past EXP-CLI-003's budget —
    the new verb is lazily loaded like every other.
  * EXP-LIFE-001 findings A (seal --dry-run writes), B (deliver needs a durable name), D (seal asserts
    containment unverifiably) and G (ref path vs canonical) are each closed or explicitly re-scoped,
    recorded append-only on that expedition.

NON-GOALS
  * No verb proliferation: one new verb, and no new lifecycle states. If a need appears that seems to
    require a second verb, it is a design failure of this one and gets reported, not built.
  * Not the CLI decomposition or the load budgets (EXP-CLI-003) — this lands on top of its registry.
  * Not dead code, dead imports or the legacy `synth migrate` removal (EXP-CLEAN-001), except that
    CLEAN-001 D6(b)'s ceremony-scope deliverable moves here and CLEAN-001 should be amended to say so.
  * Not the test infrastructure (EXP-TEST-001..005).
  * Not finding J (refinementNote is a single replaced field, so corrections overwrite what they
    correct). It is a real defect and this expedition will keep hitting it — recording findings
    against EXP-LIFE-001 requires the concatenate-don't-replace workaround — but fixing it is a
    separate change to the ledger's write model and stays out of scope here.
  * No network in read paths: `status` and `doctor` stay offline. `consolidate`, `deliver` and `seal`
    may touch the network because they are explicit write actions, and each must say so in its output.
